history.content: Hi, my phone has no signal at all—no calls, texts, or internet, and I can't send picture messages. It just shows no service.

I can help you troubleshoot this issue. First, I need to identify your account to check your line status and provide the correct support.

Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account
- Your customer ID
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD)

Once I have this information, I’ll begin diagnosing the problem.
My phone number is +1-617-555-0148 and my name is Sofia Martinez.

Your line is currently suspended, which is why you have no service for calls, texts, internet, or picture messages. However, I see that your recent bills are already paid, and your contract is still active.

Since your bills are paid and your contract is valid, I can resume your line to restore your service. After I do this, you will need to reboot your phone to regain service.

Would you like me to proceed and resume your line now?
Yes, please go ahead and resume my line.

Your line has been resumed and is now active. Please reboot your phone to restore your service for calls, texts, internet, and picture messages.

If you still experience any issues after rebooting, let me know and I can help you further.

response.result: Line LN-8830142 has been resumed and is now Active.

history.content: I rebooted my phone as you asked, but I still have no signal—no bars, no internet, and I can’t send picture messages.

Thank you for letting me know. Since your line is now active but you still have no signal, let's proceed with some troubleshooting steps to identify the cause.

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know what icons or messages you see at the top of your screen? Specifically, let me know if you see:
- An airplane icon (✈️)
- “No SIM” or “SIM error”
- “No service” or “Emergency calls only”
- Any signal bars or network type (e.g., 4G, 5G)

This information will help me guide you through the next steps.
Actually, now I see 'Excellent' signal bars, 5G, and it says 'Data Enabled' and 'Connected to Chestnut-5G' at the top of my screen. What should I try next?

That’s great news—your phone now shows excellent signal strength, 5G connectivity, and mobile data is enabled. Since you’re also connected to Wi-Fi (“Chestnut-5G”), your cellular service appears to be restored.

To confirm everything is working:
1. Try making a call and sending a regular text message (SMS).
2. Disconnect from Wi-Fi temporarily and try browsing the internet using mobile data.
3. Try sending a picture message (MMS) with Wi-Fi turned off.

If all these functions work, your service is fully restored. If you encounter any issues with calls, texts, internet, or picture messages, please let me know which specific function isn’t working, and I’ll help you troubleshoot further.
The messaging app says it can send MMS messages, but when I actually try to send a picture message with Wi-Fi off, it still doesn't go through.

Thank you for the update. Since your phone shows excellent signal, 5G, and mobile data is enabled, but MMS (picture messages) still won’t send with Wi-Fi off, let’s try the following troubleshooting steps:

1. Reset your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings to default. This often resolves MMS issues caused by incorrect network settings.
2. After resetting the APN, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings, or can you do this from your phone’s settings menu? If you need guidance, please let me know your phone’s make and model, and I’ll walk you through the steps.

I reset the APN settings and got a message saying they were set to defaults (APN: internet, MMSC URL: http://mms.carrier.com/mms). It says to reboot the device for the changes to take effect. Should I go ahead and reboot now?

Yes, please go ahead and reboot your device now. This will apply the new APN settings.

After your phone restarts, try sending a picture message (MMS) again with Wi-Fi turned off. Let me know if it works or if you still encounter any issues.
I already rebooted after resetting the APN settings, but picture messages still won't send with Wi-Fi off. The issue isn't fixed yet.

Thank you for letting me know. Since you have already reset the APN settings, rebooted your device, and still cannot send picture messages (MMS) with Wi-Fi off—despite having excellent signal and mobile data enabled—let’s try a few more steps:

1. Please check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your device. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS delivery.
   - If it is ON, please turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF and try sending a picture message again with Wi-Fi off.

Let me know if you need instructions on how to check or disable Wi-Fi Calling, or if you can do this from your phone’s settings. Once you’ve tried this, please let me know if MMS works.
Wi-Fi Calling is already off, and MMS still isn't working with Wi-Fi off. What should I try next?

Thank you for confirming that Wi-Fi Calling is off. Since you have excellent signal, mobile data enabled, APN settings reset, and Wi-Fi Calling off, but MMS still won’t send, let’s check one more thing:

The messaging app needs permission to access storage (for media files) and SMS. If these permissions are not granted, MMS may fail.

Please check your messaging app’s permissions and ensure that both “storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled. If you need instructions on how to check or enable these permissions, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can guide you.

After confirming permissions, try sending a picture message again with Wi-Fi off. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still have trouble.
Both storage and SMS permissions are already enabled for my messaging app. I tried sending a picture message again with Wi-Fi off, but it still won't send.
YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.

arguments.summary: Customer Sofia Martinez has an active line with excellent signal, 5G, and mobile data enabled. She cannot send MMS (picture messages) with Wi-Fi off, despite resetting APN settings, rebooting, confirming Wi-Fi Calling is off, and verifying messaging app permissions. All standard troubleshooting steps have been completed.
